page: OVHcloud h200-1920 is an x86_64 architecture server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 224 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz, paired with 1920.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 8.57 GB of RAM per core. The hardware configuration includes eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs from the Hopper architecture family, providing a combined total of 1128 GB of video memory. Local storage is provided by 8080 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the network interface supports a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

This server represents an ultra-dense hardware tier designed for massive parallel processing. While specific synthetic benchmark data is not available for this configuration, the inclusion of eight enterprise-grade NVIDIA H200 accelerators indicates high computational throughput for parallel workloads. The qualitative cost profile of this instance is high due to the density of premium GPU and memory resources, making it a specialized investment where resource utilization must be maximized. A potential tradeoff is the 25 Gbps network baseline, which may act as a bottleneck if massive datasets must be constantly transferred off-instance relative to the immense local processing power of the GPUs and the 8080 GB NVMe storage.

The h200-1920 is engineered for workloads that require massive GPU memory capacity and high-throughput parallel compute. Appropriate use cases include large language model training and fine-tuning, complex deep learning workloads, large-scale scientific simulations, high-performance data science pipelines, and massive parallel database operations that benefit from local NVMe storage and extensive system memory.
